archetypes.name: fixture-isolation
archetypes.rationale: This plan relies heavily on temp homes, stamps, sentinels, and fixture HOME/TMPDIR isolation where false positives are likely.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the proposed auth fixture and temp-directory setup proves the intended login versus env-key path instead of accidentally reusing stale stamps, inherited environment, or global /tmp state. Check that cleanup assertions are non-vacuous and attached to the same cases that create the temporary Codex homes or captures. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: argv-contract
archetypes.rationale: Trusted-project flags, env-key overrides, and dispatch breadcrumbs are contract-sensitive and easy to assert incompletely.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the plan’s proposed argv, sidecar, and breadcrumb assertions against the existing launcher and dispatch harness contracts. Look for missing adjacency checks, capture-file setup gaps, cases that skip Codex while still asserting Codex argv, or mismatches between probe, review-and-fix, and implementer auth semantics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash-harness-portability
archetypes.rationale: The added tests are Bash harness changes where portability and mutation-proof assertion style are central to plan quality.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the plan’s proposed shell patterns fit the existing Bash 3.2 harness idioms and avoid brittle constructs, unguarded grep counts, broad PATH stubs, or permission cleanup hazards. Check that mutation sanity checks are concrete enough to catch false-green assertions across each modified harness. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
